utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please., Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we are going to hear the witness, are there any matters that the parties would like to raise? Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I've just got one matter to raise which arose out of yesterday. Yesterday Mr. -- the witness Salko Gusic indicated in open court once in an unresponsive answer to a question and the other time in a -- at a general invitation by Your Honour at the end of his evidence that there had been some generally expressed but serious, if it were -- had the least bit of truth about it, misdemeanour by our -- our team member and likely future witness, Asim Dzambasovic. Now, that allegation, we appreciate of course that the Prosecutor would not have known it was going to be made and we -- we don't make any allegation against the Prosecutor at all in this regard. She's not here, but I just want it to be clear that this is a general policy comment. That was a hurtful and damaging comment to people, in particular the investigators, who were not able to defend themselves from it in public at the moment. They're simply here in court. It was, I take it, entirely irrelevant to the case because otherwise the Prosecutor would have sought leave to lead it in evidence in the proper and normal way. It's a matter which is of grave concern to us, that allegations like that are going to be made. Mr. Dzambasovic has been called to this Tribunal by the Prosecution in the past as a witness, and we take very seriously any allegation of this nature. But for the purpose -- the reason I trouble Your Honour with it now is because it's a matter that concerns me that is going to blow the length of the trial out, that the Defence would be concerned to deal with issues like this that are collateral issues and have nothing to do with the trial. It's my intention not to respond to those sort of attacks, and it's my intention not no deal with them because they have nothing to do with Mr. Halilovic. But because Mr. Dzambasovic has been announced in open court that it's likely he'll be a witness and because he is known to be a team member and a person who has assisted in the preparation of the case here, it's a matter that impacts. And I don't want the Court to think that merely because I'm not seeking an immediate evidentiary hearing on these allegations that we accept them. Frankly, that is the reverse of the position. We reject them, and we would want to be putting Mr. Mr. Dzambasovic forward as a person of honour and integrity when the time comes. In the meantime, what I would ask generally, both of the Prosecution and of the Court, is that all efforts are made to keep the evidence that's led relevant to the case itself and that it does not stray off. It would be improper of me at this stage to launch any attack on Mr. Gusic because he's not here, and I don't propose to say anything negative or positive about him and whatever reasons he may have had for saying what he did. Although, I point out that in relation to the question I asked, it was quite plainly a clearly unresponsive answer. But leaving aside what he says and the substance of it, I just don't want to be dealing and I don't want the Court to be dealing with bushfires and disasters which are not relevant to the case. Could I therefore put on record that the Defence does not accept what's -- what is -- what was advanced. Could I put on record that we're not proposing to deal with it as it arises and that we're going to deal with issues that relate only to Mr. Halilovic -- and not -- not sideline ones. We invite the Prosecution to do all they can to ensure that the evidence that's led in this court is relevant only to the charges, and I humbly ask the Court to have regard to what I've said, bearing in mind that on any view - the Prosecution's and the Defence's - the controversies in this case have been fought out in the press in Bosnia for a long time and battle lines have been well and truly drawn. So you might expect comments to be made, sometimes possibly, imaginably, even in good faith. And what I ask is that control be exercised over that sort of thing without prejudice to the truth or otherwise of anything that is said at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for your statement, but in the whole, as for yesterday's witness, I believe that we did pretty well, because as I said, Mr. Gusic is a very important witness. I'll give the parties enough time to do the direct and the cross-examination, and on the whole I believe that the Prosecution's direct examination was very relevant and very concise. As for the statement made by the witness at the last minute, during the testimony it's very difficult for us to know what the witness is going to say during his testimony. So since that piece of the evidence was not directly relevant to your client -- unless in the future we find some relevance of that piece of the evidence, we'll not rely on that piece of the evidence in the process of evaluating the evidence we received, and your statement has been fully recorded in the record. And I hope in the future if you found such kind of statements made by anyone which is not relevant to this case in your view, you may stand up and voice your objections. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So having said that, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Ms. Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] [Inaudible].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to make a statement?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Could we have it in B/C/S, please. Can you please instruct her to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I take an oath that I will say all the words as I should.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Mr. Re, are you ready for your direct examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Re:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Miletic.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your name Katica Miletic?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Kata Miletic. You can also say Katica. My full name is Kata Miletic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your date of birth the 13th of February, 1937?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I am now at home. I worked in a school.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Are there any problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. I've plugged in as -- as instructed to the -- to the metal white box and I've got B/C/S on two channels. Perhaps I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. In the earphone we hear the two languages simultaneously. Well, witness, I'm sorry that we have some technical problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll try this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's not seeing; it's hearing, Your Honour. I was getting two channels of B/C/S on the white box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I didn't dare switch to the other one for fear of losing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is a technical problem with one box, but I'll try and continue with this one and see how we go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But we still have the B/C/S in our earphones.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English now? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Re, can you try it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Miletic, you just told us that you're working at -- you're at home. Are you a pensioner?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live in Grabovica until 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you live in Grabovica for?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I was born in Grabovica. I never changed my place of residence until 1993. I lived there where I was born.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Shall we continue?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you live in Grabovica with until 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I lived on my own. But I had a brother and a sister-in-law in the neighbourhood, so we lived next to each other. I had my own house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your brother -- what were your brother and sister-in-law's names?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Pero and Ruza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is their family name?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Miletic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Ilka Miletic? Was Ilka Miletic a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, she is. She was, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Re, you may continue, because, you know, only if you say something that they could test the system is okay or not, and that piece of the evidence is just the background of the witness, is not that essentially important. So I believe the Defence will agree that we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Miletic, Milka Miletic, a relative, was she a cousin of yours?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Ljubija -- sorry, Ljubica Mandic and Andrija Mandic? Are they related to you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I know them. Ljubica was related to me, but Andrija wasn't. I knew them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Ivan Mandic? Who's he?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: That's Ljubica's brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in Grabovica in May 1993 when soldiers came to the village?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To which army did these soldiers belong?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: From Sarajevo. The Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that they were from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I know that because they wore military uniforms. Zuka was there, general and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was Zuka from?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably from Sarajevo. But I have no idea. I just heard rumours about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you living in Grabovica in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened in early September 1993 in relation to soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Between the 8th and the 9th, or just before the 8th, many more soldiers came. And between the 8th and 9th, there was a massacre in Grabovica and 33 Croats were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you see -- first see the soldiers in September 1993? I'm sorry, I withdraw that. When did you see the -- first see the many more soldiers who came in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you the exact date. It was about a week before the massacre. About a week before the night between the 8th and the 9th. But I can't tell you the precise date. I don't want to lie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were these soldiers wearing, these new soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Multicoloured military clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any military insignia on their clothes?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They did have some kind of insignia, but I didn't really look at the insignia. I didn't pay attention to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of these soldiers stay in the village or were accommodated in the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the right bank, and there were checkpoints. They arrived on the right bank about a week before the massacre. We lived on the left bank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you know there were houses on the right bank of Grabovica. Were the soldiers staying in those houses or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: There were huts, sheds. There were houses. There were all kinds of buildings there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were the soldiers staying?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: In huts or in houses. There were huts there belonging to the electric plant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these soldiers from the same army - that's the ABiH - as the soldiers who came in May 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: The same ones who took Grabovica in May. They were the same people. But I can't really say. I'm not really that well informed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the name of Zuka before as the -- I think you said general in charge of the soldiers who were there from May 1993. Do you know or did you hear anything about whether Zuka had anything to do with the soldiers who were there in -- the new soldiers who were there in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I don't know if he was there in 1993. I don't know who was connected to whom. I can't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any difference between the behaviour of the troops who -- the soldiers who came in May 1993 in relation to the civilians in Grabovica and the behaviour of those who came in September 1993 in relation to the civilians in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I don't know. There weren't any changes there. I could see something was going on. There were more soldiers. But I don't know about any other changes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you on the 8th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: At my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the soldiers doing on that day? What did you see the soldiers or hear the soldiers doing?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They told us to go. We were on the left bank, and we set out towards Jablanica. We passed through alive. We were in the museum for six months, until we were exchanged. This was after six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 8th of September, you were at your house and soldiers told you that you had to go. That --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 9th, we came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: In the morning. On the 9th, in the morning. We were at home on the 8th. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. I just -- I want to ask you or clarify what happened or what you saw or heard in Grabovica on the 8th of September; that's the day before you left the village. You said there were some soldiers who told you that you had to go. Where did the soldiers --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Excuse me. I object to that. There's a -- sorry, could the witness just excuse me for one moment while I make the objection. Pardon me. The objection is that that was -- there was a leading proposition in there about what was said on the 8th. Now, the witness hasn't agreed to that, and I object to it being put to the witness that she was told anything by soldiers on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'd just point my friend -- my learned friend to the transcript at page -- point 17: What did the soldiers -- see the soldiers or hear them doing? Answer: They told us to go. I was just leading from that. She said, "They told us to go."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's quite plain, it's obvious from the context of that that she was giving an answer that was not limited to the 8th. She talked about events six months later in that answer. Now, Your Honour, my friend is entitled to lead the evidence if it's the evidence. But he should ask the witness and not tell her that she was told anything on the 8th, because that's a matter of potential significance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness told us that, you know, she was asked to go away at that time, but I see that this question is a compound question. Maybe, Mr. Re, you could break it. Ask her one question after another and build up your case step by step.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Miletic, did the soldiers who told you to go tell you on the 8th or at the 9th? These were the soldiers from the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: On the 9th, all the soldiers were at the checkpoint. I don't know which ones they were. On the 9th, to be clear, we left our homes. On the 9th we set off from our houses. On the 9th of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You set out on the 9th. Did the soldiers at the checkpoint tell you that you had to go on the 8th or the 9th?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: On the 9th. On the 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers in the village on the 8th and the 9th, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Every soldier has a -- a rifle on his shoulder; otherwise, they wouldn't be a soldier without a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear or see any soldiers using their weapons on the 8th; that's the day before you left? Did you hear any shooting?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I don't know. These were combat operations. You could always hear shooting. I don't know who was shooting. It's war. It doesn't really matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just to clarify your last answer. I'm asking you about the 8th of September, when you were at home. Do you remember hearing any shooting - and I'm talking about from the village of Grabovica - either on your side of the river or the other side?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. From the other side, yes, you could hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in the day or in the night or both?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: You could hear it by day and by night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe its length and intensity? For example, was it an occasional shot, shooting all day, a burst here and there, or what?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Occasionally. Sometimes you could hear a rifle shot. Occasionally. I can say that quite clearly, that it was occasional.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other sounds could you hear from the soldiers, apart from the shooting across the river on the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They were singing. At night you could hear singing. That's all I heard. I could hear nothing else. That the soldiers were singing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you heard the soldiers singing. Did you hear -- could you hear other people, people apart from the soldiers, making noises on the night of the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't really hear anything. I couldn't really differentiate between the sounds, what they were saying, what this noise was. I don't know who was doing what. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you stay in your house or stay in that house on night of the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, until the morning of the 9th. In the morning of the 9th, we left our homes at 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before leaving your home at about 1500 hours, what did you do during the day in the village? Were you at home? Did you go somewhere? Did you see anyone?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I went to see my sister. I could see that something was uncomfortable, something was wrong, so I went to see what was going on. And then I went back home, and then we set off for Jablanica on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is your sister's house from where you were staying?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: About 900 metres. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your sister, is that Ljubica?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, your sister, was that the sister Ljubica you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's my sister. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us you heard shooting on the day and night before. That's on the 8th of September. Did you hear or see the soldiers shooting in the morning of the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there was occasional shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on the same side of the river you were on or the other side of the river?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: This was on the right bank. We were on the left side and the shooting was on the right side of the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what direction was the -- what direction was the fire directed or the shooting directed?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know where the shooting was. I didn't even dare look. I have no idea. I would run into the house. I don't know anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything to suggest there were -- there was firing overhead of your house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was over the houses. One bullet was fired above the house, but I don't know about the other things. I really didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bullet that was fired over your house, was that in the morning or the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: It was in the morning, around 9.00, on the 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went and visited your sister Ljubica. Did you also visit Ilka Miletic, your cousin, on the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went to see my sister at about 10.00, and I could see she's not around the river. Then I saw Ilka. Her close -- house is close by. And then I saw that she was okay, and then I went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your brother's wife at home when you arrived back?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was she doing?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: She was preparing to leave, she and my brother. And I said, "What is going on?" And she said, "Well, these refugees told us to go if you mean to stay alive."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've described soldiers shooting on the other side of the river. Did any soldiers come near your house when you were there, before you left?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they did. They came to the house when we were leaving. Yes, they did come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these soldiers from the same army - that's the ABiH - as the soldiers from the other side of the river?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, exactly. The Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the soldiers say to you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Well, to go. To go, to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you why you had to leave?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They didn't say anything about why we should leave. Just told us to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these soldiers like the other soldiers you saw, armed?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They were all armed. All of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many soldiers came to your house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: A large number of them, but I don't know the exact number. I cannot lie to you. I don't -- I'm not a person to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What could you tell about where they were from from their accents?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They were from Sarajevo, but I don't know where they were from. But the soldiers were from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give them anything?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They took what was there. They did and we did too. They took whatever they needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just elaborate on that a bit more. What did the soldiers do when they came -- came to your house? You said they told you to go, but what else did they do?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They were looking through things, searching through the house. I don't know what to say. They were looking for something. They were rummaging through the house. I don't know what they were looking for. And then we left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few moments ago I asked you whether you gave them anything, and you said, "They took what was there. They took whatever they needed." What I'm asking you is: Did you give them anything --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Whatever they needed. Yes, I did. I had some money. It wasn't a lot of money. I gave it to them and we left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how much money was it you gave them?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: 500 German marks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, "We left." Who was "we"?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: My brother, my sister-in-law, and I, the three of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you have with you? Were you carrying anything?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Coats, jackets, a bag, shoes and so on. A few things, some underwear and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you leave on foot?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: We took the main road towards Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to pass Ilka Miletic's house to get there?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Ilka at her house when you went past, as you were leaving the village?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other people around her house when you went past it or in the vicinity of her house when you went past it?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there was some refugees there, soldiers as well. But I don't know exactly who was there, but yes, there were people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were they doing, these people, these refugees and soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I don't know. They were just sitting there talking. We passed by along the road on our way towards Jablanica. And there were also some other people there. There was some recording. There was a camera there or something. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean a video? Mrs. Miletic, do you mean a video camera? You said there was a camera and some recording. Are you referring to a video camera?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? Yes, probably. I don't know what it was. They were recording from a small TAM truck, but I don't know what they were doing. They were recording something on the right side. There was a small TAM truck there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "they," are you referring to the soldiers or the refugees?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Soldiers. They were soldiers. No, not the refugees. These were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The small TAM truck, did you notice anything about its number plates or where they were from?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: The registration plates were from Sarajevo, Sarajevo registration plates. I can tell you that, but I can't tell you anything else about the vehicle. But it had Sarajevo registration plates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you walk to?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Along the main road that goes from Grabovica, Mostar, Jablanica. We were going towards Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see as you walked towards Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: When we were a distance away from the village, I don't know where, but that's where the dam is; that's where we saw Ilka's dead body, this -- Miletic, but we didn't really dare look at it too closely. Ivan Mandic also we passed and went to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw Ilka's dead -- Ilka Miletic's dead body and you said you also saw Ivan Mandic. Was Ivan Mandic alive or dead when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: He was dead. Both of them were dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the bodies in relation to each other? How close or far apart were they?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I didn't really notice that. They were just lying beside the road. But I don't know how far apart they were. I really don't know. We were in danger, so I really don't know. They were together, but I don't know how far apart the bodies were. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you didn't dare look at it too closely. Do you mean you just kept on walking to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you walk all the way to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, up to Donja Jablanica. Then a car stopped for us and picked us up and we got in and we were driven to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Ilka Miletic and Ivan Mandic, were either of those people soldiers or were they both civilians?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They were both civilians. He was an elderly man suffering from asthma. She was an elderly woman, quite -- older. She lived by herself. She didn't have anyone. She was not married. They were both elderly and not in good health. They didn't have any weapons or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were either of them taking part in combat activities, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: No. No. She was born in 1927. There's no way that they could have been in combat. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to show the witness a photograph which is Exhibit -- MFI162, 04020972. I'm just not sure how we can show the witness and get her to mark on it if it's going to be broadcast on the screen. We'll have to do some scribing, I think. It's in Sanction at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid that it can't be done through the videolink, to ask -- I mean to ask the witness to mark on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can a photo be placed on the ELMO and the witness be asked to point on the screen in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Miletic, I'm putting a photograph on the screen, and I want you to have a look at it. I'm going to ask you to point out things. And point -- point to things on this particular photo with a pen or some other pointy object.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the photograph?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recognise it as a photograph -- an overhead photograph of -- sorry, of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: This is my own village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I want you to point to where your -- can you see your house on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you just excuse me one moment, please. We have the photograph up on the screen, but we don't have a pointer being shown at this stage. I'm not sure if we're seeing what the witness is seeing or if we're seeing a view from -- live from her viewing box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You're much luckier than I am because I didn't see the picture on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's excellent.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Excuse me, Your Honour. But it's impossible for the witness to point to any location on the map due to how we're situated here in Sarajevo. The screen is away from the witness, so we -- it's difficult for her to be able to point. If there is a picture here that we could get perhaps with one of the lawyers being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, would you please ask the witness to point to that picture again. We'll see whether we can see it or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Miletic, can you see your house on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. I can see all the houses. Yesterday I told the man in the hotel. I showed him all the houses and who was killed. I don't know if there's any use in saying it again. I showed it. I pointed it out to him with a pencil, that lawyer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you have a copy of that photograph there with you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: No. It's with the lawyer in the hotel. That's my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Maybe you can describe it for us. If you look at the photograph, the river goes through the middle of the -- the photograph. Is your house on the top side of the photograph on the screen?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: No. My house is at the beginning, and Ilka's house is near the top there, Ilka Miletic, and the others and Ljubica's. And mine is down here at the beginning of the village. I can see them all. Theirs are up there, about 900 metres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you divide the screen into four, there's a top left, top right, bottom left, and bottom right. I want you to -- I want you to imagine that. Where is your -- where is the house you were staying in in September 1993? Is it in the bottom left of the screen or bottom right of the screen?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: It's in the lower left-hand corner of the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When you walked towards Jablanica, can you tell us in relation to the photo, did you walk towards the left or the right of the photo? That's towards the dam, which is on the right, or down the river, which is on the left?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: We went along the river, along the main road on the left bank. There's only one right direction. You can see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that towards the dam or away from the dam? Which way did you walk? To the left or to the right as you look at this --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Towards the dam, upstream. We went along the left bank toward the dam. That's the main road leading to Jablanica and then on to Sarajevo. It's on the left bank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that's the road you can -- is that the road you can see which is just next to the river, going upstream towards the dam? Is that the road you took?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. You can see it on the screen. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the screen, in about the very middle on the left bank you can see what looks like a large sandbank as the river bends towards the dam. Can you just look at that area.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want you to -- look at the -- look at the -- look at the map -- look at the screen and tell the Trial Chamber where it was you saw the two bodies, Ilka Miletic and Ivan Mandic.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: When you pass by this big embankment - or what can I call it - there's Ilka's house that's marked on the screen now, and then there are a few metres further to go to the dam, where we saw her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said Ilka's house is there. Can you just describe for us which one Ilka's house is? We've enlarged a bit and there seems to be about four or five houses near that sandbank. Was it one of those ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, but I can't see what's been enlarged and what's been shown to the witness. I just have a static image in front of me here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, because of the technical problems, you know, and the -- we could not do everything as we did in this courtroom, I think that, you know, there's no disputes that, you know, those two people's dead bodies were found in the village or nearby the village, so there's no need for us to know the exact location of those dead bodies. Do you agree, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately, with respect, I don't. It does matter where they were. But, however, the Prosecutor is entitled to do what he's doing now. And I'm not objecting to him doing it. I just wanted to -- I just want to know where he says they were and where the witness says they were. And it might be -- it might be able to be done by oral description using this photograph. My only concern was that I didn't have the same photograph in front of me or the same part of the photograph to which Mr. Re was referring, and therefore as long as I've got in front of me what he's referring to, I'm content and I'm happy with the way he's proceeding, frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll see how far we could go. As a matter of fact, I only have the overall pictures but not, you know, zoomed pictures on my screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Miletic, can you just describe where Ilka Miletic's house is in relation to that sandbank. Is it above or below the sandbank, to the left or the right on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: You see those huts? It's right behind them. There are three small houses there. One belonged to her aunt. And there they are, in front of those huts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these the three or four buildings which are just underneath -- slightly to the left and underneath the sandbank in the bend in the river?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Those two, three houses at the bend -- no, no, they're a bit lower down. Can you see the huts? There are eight of them, and then right behind the huts, not ten steps away, that's where her house is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to be clear on which huts you're referring to. Are these the -- the huts that go up the hillside, the long ones?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: On the left bank, near the asphalt road. That's where the huts are. When you're going in the direction of Sarajevo, they're on your right-hand side, but apparently in these papers it's called the left bank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Approximately how far from the sandbank in metres is Ilka Miletic's house and these huts?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: There they are, below the sandbank. They're in the village. You know what the village is? They're in the village, in the middle of the village. That's the easiest. It's down by the asphalt road. I did show that to that man in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there an area in that photograph that you describe as a lake?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. There's the lake. It's the River Neretva, but you can call it a lake. It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were leaving -- leaving on the -- the 9th, did you see soldiers doing anything near the lake?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were joking. They were shooting into the lake, maybe shooting at fish. I don't know what they were doing. I have no idea. I just saw them by the lake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the body of Ilka Miletic or -- and Ivan Mandic were ever recovered or identified?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Ilka's was never -- it's hard for me to pronounce. Ivan's was. He was buried in Mostar and then taken back to Grabovica, where his wife is buried. That's what the children did when they were able to. But Ilka's was never found. I -- I am sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say when Ivan Mandic's body was identified?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you the date. I can't lie. I really can't. Was it 1995? I don't know. I can't tell you precisely. I don't like lying. I don't know the precise date. You can ask somebody who knows better than I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's the evidence in chief, unless a photograph could be obtained and -- the photograph which apparently was shown to her yesterday could be obtained and shown to her again in Sarajevo. That's as far as I can take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, is it possible to show this witness some photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In court or in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In both places, wherever.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's possible for her to have a photograph in front of her in Sarajevo and mark on that and it to be shown to the -- the screen, I think, and tendered and given to the registry officer and brought back here. I think I've seen that done before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In general, there's no objections to anything that's going to help. I'm not sure what's planned here. But can I indicate that I would intend to take the witness for a walk up this -- up this road in this photograph and attempt to step by step show what she passed and that might suffice? That would be my intention. And I was also going to show her certain photographs and get her to identify things without marking on them. But I don't object to any realistic proposal. Frankly, the best proposal seems to me that the witness should have had or should have the photograph with her in Sarajevo and can mark what she wants and then that can be tendered in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let us try.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We have to telephone the court in -- or the office in Sarajevo and find the photograph, which I believe should be there.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Your Honours, can you hear me? Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I was told that the witness there needs some preparations, so maybe we could have a break at this stage. So we'll have 30 minutes' break and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Chana, you have something to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In respect to the next witness, whose name I will not now speak in public, she has requested for protective measures, Your Honour. She would like pseudonym and face distortion. I have discussed with her at some length, and this was done yesterday by our -- our man in Sarajevo, as we can call him, and this morning I talked to her myself. She says that she would like protection because they still own a home in Grabovica and her husband and her do return there on the odd occasion and she feels that she had been all the time under the illusion that she will be given protective measures, and I promised to ask Your Honours whether that would be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any comments on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, as we've indicated in the past, we take a different view with people who are genuinely victims, as she is, and if it is a matter of setting her at her ease to have those matters, of course it's the Court's decision, but we make no submission against it being done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Your request is granted, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Most obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Re, I believe that the photographs are in place. Are you going to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Miletic, do you have the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is that the same photograph that the lawyer showed you yesterday and which you marked but the one you have now is a blank one?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: It's the same. Yes, here it is before me on paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Does it have the number 02992354 at the very top of it?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's, for the record, MFI163.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want you to -- first of all, it's a photocopy of -- it's a black-and-white photocopy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to mark four things on this photograph for me with a circle and "1", "2", "3", and "4". Firstly, I want you to draw on the map, on the plan, your own house with a "1". Put a "1" inside the circle. And tell me when you've done that.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I've done that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number "2", the house of Ilka Miletic; the same, a circle with a "2" inside it.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I've done that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 3, the house of Ivan Mandic; the same, a circle with a "3" on it.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I've done that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, number 4, a circle and the spot where the bodies were.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Number 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just so this photograph is completely clear, can you put -- is there a white --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I've done that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there a white space underneath the photograph where you can write?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, around the edges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just, please, put "1", "2", "3", and "4", and next to "1", put your name, Katica Miletic.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. "1", "2", "3", "4", in a sequence? Right next to each other?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However it fits.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then my name, Miletic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I've done that. I've written down the numbers and my name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Number 2, "Ilka Miletic"; and number 3, "Ivan Mandic?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Their names?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Next to "2", "Ilka Miletic," and next to "3", "Ivan Mandic."

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I've done that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- show the photograph to the screen so we can have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Where am I supposed to put it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] You're not going to be able to actually see it, I don't think, the markings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just move it down a bit so we can see the number 4. Maybe I meant up, the other way.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Do you want them to zoom in?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can't actually see the number 4 on that photograph. Could you please describe where it is. Someone -- anyone who's holding it, would you be able to point to where the number 4 is on the photograph so we can see it. Thank you. May that be received into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the court deputy could give it a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, before it's received into evidence, there's just one matter. I was going to ask a question. It may be that Mr. Re could ask the question. I just wanted to ask that -- that it be marked where Ljubica Mandic's house was as well. And if we don't mark it now, we're going to have to get it to do -- to get another copy and tender that. So -- the Prosecution is not obliged to, but it may be appropriate that they could ask that that be done and then I won't oppose the tender at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I think that's --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Mandic -- sorry, Mrs. Miletic, could you also mark on that photograph the house of Ljubica Mandic, please, if it's there. Please do that with a "5" and a circle.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And please, at the very bottom, can you just write the "5" and "Ljubica Mandic," please, for the legend.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And when that's done, can that please again be shown to the screen. And it would help if someone could point to where the "5" is. Thank you. I've finished with that diagram or photograph. May it be now received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What's the number for that, Mr. Court Deputy?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P163, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Morrissey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Miletic, my name is Morrissey, and I am Defence counsel for Mr. Halilovic in this matter. I have a short number of questions for you, and the first questions I want to ask are about the moment when you saw the bodies of the deceased people that you noticed on the road to Jablanica. Now, as you walked along that road towards Jablanica, were the bodies that you saw to your left, on the river side, or were they to your right?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: On the left side of the river as you go towards Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they on the hillside leading down to the river or were they still on the road?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Next to the road. Next to the asphalt road. The river is down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Miletic, I want to put to you something that you told the investigators from this Tribunal in the past, and then I'm going to ask you if it's accurate and ask you some questions. So if you would just have patience, I'll read this to you briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And Your Honours, could I indicate that what I'm reading from is a statement here provided to the Defence, a statement -- an ICTY statement of this witness dated 31st of July, 2003 and given to an interviewer named Bernard Brun, and I'm reading from page 2, paragraph 8 of the -- of the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I shall read you this passage. And you were talking about your cousin -- sorry, your sister-in-law -- your cousin Ilka. And you said this: "I never seen her alive again, but I think I saw her body while I was walking on the main road toward Jablanica. At -- sorry, around 1500 hours, I saw two bodies along the main road on the left side close to the dam."

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, there's just a little bit more. I want to keep reading. Okay. So now I'm quoting again: "I suppose that those bodies belonged to Ilka Miletic and Ivan Mandic because they were in civilian clothings -- clothes and had grey hair. I didn't dare to watch the bodies closer because at the same time soldiers were around." Now, Ms. Miletic, did you say that to the investigators and -- and is that the truth?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did say it, and it is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, let me ask you some questions about this. When you saw those bodies, you did not stop to inspect them to identify them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I understand that that is because you were very upset and nervous about what might happen to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it therefore that you didn't stop working but you continued as quickly as you could towards Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the same time you passed those two bodies, you were unable to be sure of their identity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: How do you mean? Could you please repeat that, identify. I don't understand that sentence. Could you please repeat that, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I shall put the question a slightly different way. Today in court you have expressed the view that the two people you saw were Ilka Miletic and Ivan Mandic. There's no criticism of you --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in that view, but my question is: At the very moment when you walked past those two bodies that you saw, at that moment you did not know precisely who those two people were. Now, do you agree with the proposition I've just put?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I knew who they were, but we just didn't dare. I didn't have time nor was I able to go closer. We just passed by, and they were left behind. What could I have done? There was nothing I could do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can I make it quite clear that there is no criticism of you at all. That's not what these questions are about. But let me ask some more questions: When you walked past those bodies, you did not look at the face of either of them; is that true?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: We just passed by. There was this woman in front of me -- well, she had a -- a grey sheepskin or fur coat. She had grey hair. What more could I see?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that you should have seen anything more, but that is in fact what you saw and what you noticed; am I right?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as that woman that you saw, I take it, then, you saw the back of her head; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: She was lying down. I didn't pay attention to the back of her head. She was lying there dead. I just passed by. She's an elderly woman, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you didn't make any observations of other clothes, apart from the sheepskin coat; is that true?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I didn't really look much more. She had a brown fur coat. I didn't really look. She was wearing trousers, of course. I don't know. It's been 11 years since then. I don't know what colour the trousers were or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. But is this true that because of the condition of fear and danger you were in, you looked at her for no more than two seconds?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: That is true, yes. Yes. For sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I turn now to the -- the male person that you saw. Did you look at this male person for a similar period of time, one to two seconds?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: The same. Yes, the same. He was a sick person. He was suffering from asthma. I don't know what else to tell you. Both of them were there dead. They both had grey hair. They were elderly people. What more can I say? I have nothing further to add.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Ms. Miletic, at that time as you walked along the road, were you wearing your glasses or not?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: No. No, I wasn't. I was younger then. It's been 11 years since then. I wasn't wearing glasses then at that time. I can tell you that for sure. That's a positive thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. Let me just clarify that question. And it's not meant to be a rude question. At that time, were you in the habit of wearing glasses at all, or is that something that you have adopted more recently?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I hadn't started to wear glasses at that time, no. I have been wearing glasses since four years ago. For the past four years, I've been wearing glasses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, upon arriving in Jablanica --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upon arriving in Jablanica, did you hear some news that -- well, I withdraw that question. I just want to confirm this. You have answered this question and I just want to be clear that I've understood the answer, okay? As to -- as to the woman that you saw, you did not actually see her face at that time you saw her; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I did. I am positive that it was her. I saw her face. She was lying there. But we just walked by quickly. I've known this woman for a long, long time. It wasn't difficult for me to recognise her, but we didn't spend any time there. This is my cousin, my relative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that. But Ms. Miletic, in your statement which I read out to you, you used this term. You said: "I suppose that those bodies belonged to Ilka Miletic and Ivan Mandic because they were in civilian clothes and had grey hair." Now, you recall I asked you about that and you said that was the truth? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. So it is the fact, isn't it, that you did not get a good look at the face of this woman that you saw?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I did. I walked past her. I looked and then continued on my way. What else could I do? What else could I have done? I have no further comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. The people that you were with walking along the road, did you make the comment to them, "Look, that's Ilka. Look, that's Ivan," or did you not make that comment?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: No. No. We didn't go there. These were elderly people. We just kept walking by. We were just -- we continued walking. We didn't have any comments or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In your statement, why was it, then, that you said the word "I suppose" at the start of the statement, "I suppose that those bodies belonged to Ilka Miletic and Ivan Mandic"?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Because I saw her. I saw her. I saw them, and we walked past them. We were on our way to Jablanica. We passed by them, and they remained there. That's why I said it. I didn't make that up. I'm not telling you a lie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Miletic, no one is suggesting that you're telling us a lie. Now, could I ask you some general questions, please, about the situation in your village prior to the killings that -- that bring us here. First of all, after the Bosnian army came to Grabovica on the 9th of May, did a group of soldiers known as Cedo's Wolves take up residence in the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They would come and go all the time to our village. When the B and H army took control of our village on the 10th of May, they were there. They were walking around. I was not paying attention to what they were doing. I was minding my own business. But I have no -- I have no other comment. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In general terms, did you keep to yourself and not mix with the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: When they would ask us something, we would respond to their questions. If they saw us around our house or something, if they asked us a question, we would give them an answer if we knew it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Late in August, did a large number of refugees begin to pass through Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And did some of those refugees come to stay in the village?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you and -- and some of those that you know from the village extend kindness to them and from time to time give them food and friendship?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We took care of them very well for that first week, and there were even people that we knew who had come to our villages, refugees. We were very nice to those people. A week later, when the massacre took place, we left, so we didn't really see them anymore. But during that week when we were together, our conduct towards them was very nice. But that's about all I can say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, at around that time, did the Bosnian army provide a medical doctor to provide services to the Grabovica people at the power plant facility?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, during the summer. That is true. From May until right up to the massacre on the 9th of September, yes. But really once we left, I don't know anything that was happening there. I really don't. I've said that sincerely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's okay. That's okay. The questions focus on that period in the summer and up until the time when you left, okay? Did the army also provide a weekly bus service that took people from the village into Jablanica for shopping and other purposes?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They said that they would do that, but I don't really remember. But there weren't really too many buses around. I really don't know. They did say that, but there weren't many buses. Maybe there was a shortage of fuel or something, but I really don't know much about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, when those refugees came to live in the village, do you remember an elderly man among those refugees with the name of Zulfo?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Was that a civilian? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The evidence -- well, we think it will be, but in any event if you don't recall him, that's okay. Do you recall that some refugees --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall that some refugees were housed with Ivan and Stoja Pranjic on the right bank?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't know who that was, to tell you the truth. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is -- is your memory this: That there were some refugees housed on the right bank but you can't be sure in which house or with which people?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. We're divided. The river divides us, so I don't know who was on the right bank of the refugees. I don't know. That's what we call it, the right bank. I don't know if any of the refugees were there. I really cannot recall. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Ms. Miletic, you've already given evidence as to what happened on the 8th and the early part of the 9th of September, and I'm not going to repeat or take you over that evidence again. So I want to come, however --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to come to the point at which you set out on your journey and just indicate the path that you took.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: From my house?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Now, just tell me if these facts are accurate. We'll go through them and you can comment. First of all, the -- the three of you left from your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After about 900 metres, you passed the house of Ilka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And soon after that, you passed the house of Ljubica Mandic.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in passing the house of Ljubica Mandic, was she at home?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention. We walked by quickly. I really don't know. We were in a hurry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were close to Ljubica Mandic, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. But we were in a hurry. We were really in a hurry. I didn't go into the house or pay attention to that because the impression that we had came from one of the soldiers. He told us, "Hurry up." That's all I can say. So that's why we were in a hurry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that you were in a hurry. Is it also the fact that as you passed the area where Ljubica's house is, a Muslim refugee told you, "They've gone already," or words to that effect?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Nobody said anything to me. I don't want to lie. This is a court and I don't want to say anything that is not true. Nobody told me that they had left, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, the -- the reason you were hurrying is, quite frankly, because you were afraid that you might be hurt or killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We were afraid. You were never feeling safe with the army around, so it's true that we were afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But on this occasion, you were afraid of death; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Of course. That is very normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can I ask you this: Why didn't you take the ten seconds or so needed to knock on Ljubica's door and see if she was there?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't. I didn't have time. I was afraid. I didn't dare to do that, and that's it. We were in a hurry, so I didn't knock on the door, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're sure that no Muslim refugee told you that all these people -- that they were all gone or that everybody had left?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I did meet one woman. I asked her, "Where are our women?" And she said, "They're all gone." But this was a woman. I didn't know that woman. She was a refugee. But I did ask her, "Tell me, please, where are all of our women?" And she said, "They're all -- they've all gone," and that's how it ended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And it's because of that that you didn't waste time knocking on doors and seeing where people were.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I didn't knock, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You pressed on towards Jablanica in the belief that Ljubica had already gone.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And -- Yes. Excuse me a moment. I've just got a question about the soldiers who came to your house and told you to leave. Did those -- did you see what direction those soldiers came from? The Mostar direction or the Jablanica direction, in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Jablanica. From the right bank. They were not from Mostar. I am sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Not from that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm really referring to their approach to your house, not their original place of residence.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: From the direction of the north, from Jablanica. There are no other directions where we are. There is north and south. South is from Mostar and north is from Jablanica, and they came from Jablanica. I don't know how to explain it to you any other way. I'm not able to explain it in any other way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've explained it perfectly, and thank you. There is -- at the southern end of the village of Grabovica, there was once an old iron footbridge. Was that still in place at the time of these incidents?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But pedestrians didn't dare to do that. Perhaps a younger man or something, but it's quite bad. It's -- it's a rotting bridge and it was not in good condition, and nobody really dared to cross it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just going to ask you to -- to look at a couple of photographs now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I ask that the witness be shown -- just excuse me a moment -- photograph -- I apologise for this, but I don't have the MFI number. Your Honours, I'm sorry about this. I'll have to just give the old numbers. I thought I had it marked, but I don't. This is Prosecution photograph P81, and the four numbers are 01494688.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That would be P81, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, it's admitted. Yes. I'm sorry, I had a failure of confidence in my numbering system. It is admitted as P81. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This photograph that's going to be shown to you, Ms. Miletic, is an aerial view of some houses. And I just want you to look at them. Do you have that photograph in front of you yet?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] We do not have the photograph. It's being shown now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Miletic, do you see in that photograph in the top left-hand corner an L-shaped building with a grey roof?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there soldiers billeted in that building?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, those huts you can see below the buildings, they belonged to the hydroelectric power plant. That's where they were billeted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the house that's on the main road on the left-hand side of the picture, is that the house owned by Luca and Jozo Mandic?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Luca and Jozo Mandic? Oh, yes. Yes, you can see it. Yes. I recall it now. When you go from Mostar on the left-hand side, there is a little hut there for -- for curing meat. I don't know what you call it. Yes, you can see that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Now, on the right-hand side, can you see some houses which are at the start of a very small narrow valley?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.
