utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in that valley --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If Your Honour -- if you would just excuse me a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll withdraw that question. In relation to that valley there, can you explain whereabouts was the refugee that you saw who told you, "They've all gone"?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: She was going down the road into the village. It's a street. She was walking down the street and so was I. And I don't know how I addressed her, but I said, "Where are our people?" And she said, "They've left." But it's this street branching off into the village, and that's where we met and that's where she spoke to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that -- is that point at which you met or is that street in which you met shown in this photograph that you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: No. It's going from Jozo's house towards the south, about some 10 metres to the south. You can't see that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll show you another photograph, and we'll see if you can indicate it.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Excuse me, Mr. Morrissey, but it's -- I want you to know that if you want her to point to any parts on the picture, she can. We've set it up so that she can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, perhaps I -- perhaps I won't need to show you another photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've indicated that it is 10 metres to the left-hand side of the edge of this photograph that you're looking at; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. But towards the south, towards the south. Not towards the north.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, towards Mostar.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's right. How silly of me not to say that. It's in the direction of Mostar, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Miletic, would you just bear with me for one moment. This cross-examination has almost finished.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead. Just go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. When you were collected by the -- when you arrived at Donja Jablanica, you were picked up in a vehicle by -- by some men, and I wanted to ask you --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- do you -- were those men policemen?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: I don't know. They had multicoloured clothes. I don't want to lie. They stopped. I'm grateful to them. We got in, my brother and brother-in-law and myself. We didn't talk at all. They just asked us where we wanted to go, and I told them to drop us off at the petrol station, and that's what happened. And who they were, I don't know. They stopped at the petrol station and let us out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In -- near to the area where you saw the two bodies that you noticed, is there a small channel for water?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: There's a dam there. The dam is a bit upstream from that place, but it's a bit further up from my house, and there are channels there. There may be a spring of water. I don't know. I never walked around there much. Somebody else who lived closer to that place might be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The final question relates to the vehicle that you saw when you saw the soldiers with the video camera. Could you describe that vehicle, please.

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: It was a TAM truck. It was the colour of an orange. I don't know what you'd call that colour. It's like an orange. We call that kind of truck a Tamic. That's all I can tell you about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you seen that truck being used -- that truck or trucks of that sort being used by the soldiers in the previous months?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. They drove around in it. They didn't have many trucks, but they did drive around. What do I know? I didn't really look. I just know that they did drive around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. All I'm asking you about is that you'd seen trucks like this over the previous months in use by the soldiers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much for your patience.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Those are the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Re-examined by Mr. Re:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Miletic --

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey asked you about the clothes that Ilka Miletic was wearing when you saw her body on your way to Jablanica. You said she was wearing a brown sheepskin coat. Had you seen her wearing that brown sheepskin coat before?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey also asked you about refugees. What was the ethnicity of the refugees in Grabovica in August and September 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: They were Muslims by nationality. That's all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are a Bosnian Croat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I am a Catholic. I am a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your relatives, Ilka Miletic, she likewise was a Bosnian Croat, is that correct, and Ivan Mandic?

utterances.speaker: KATICA MILETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, thank you very much, witness, for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too. You have been very nice to me. I don't know whether I was nice to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the Bench will wish you a good journey back home today. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you again. Thank you very much. I wish you good luck in your work and in everything and a long life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that we have a few minutes left for this sitting. Are there any matters that the parties would like to raise at this stage? Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only matter that comes immediately to mind is the list of witnesses for next week. The Prosecution has indicated orally certain matters this morning, but I think it should be spelled out now who is coming and in what order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course, because, you know, we have some delay, you know, for this week. The two witnesses as requested by the Prosecutor has been postponed until next week. Maybe it's time for the Prosecution to let us know what's the order for the next witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will file it in writing. The parent order, or the order that we believe is set has to go to the Victims and Witnesses Unit to contact the persons. But what it appears to be is Dr. Definis-Gojanovic will be first because of scheduling. We want to get her on and off and back to the hospital; that next we would have Mr. Arnautovic, who was scheduled initially to be on this week; then Mr. Mehinovic, who was supposed to be on this week; and then I just want to check the next two with the Victims and Witnesses Unit. One of those two might -- is requesting protective measures or was initially requesting, so I'd rather not say the names in public, but there will be a list as soon as I speak -- confirm with the Victims and Witnesses Unit, so within the next hour or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I believe that we'll receive that list as early as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think there are a few issues I have to deal with. The first one is that I would like to draw the attention of the parties that this Trial Chamber granted the Prosecution's motion to vary its Rule 65 ter witness list. Referring to the order of the Trial Chamber in its decision on the variation of the witness list to disclose the 66(A)(ii) material concerning -- concerning the witnesses added to the Prosecution's witness list, the Trial Chamber thereby grants the Prosecution's application for leave to disclose the Rule 66(A)(ii) material pursuant to the Trial Chamber's decision of 7 May filed on the 17th January 2005 concerning with the four statements given by Delalic, and the Prosecution's request for leave to disclose statement pursuant to 7th May 2004, the Trial Chamber's order filed on the 26th January 2005, the one statement concerning a witness. Maybe we could do it in the private session if it's requested by the parties. An order of the Prosecution to provide the statement to the Defence in English translation if not already done so. As said in the decision, the Trial Chamber will ensure that Defence has adequate time to prepare for the added witnesses. Well, I think that's all for today, and then tomorrow we'll have another witness through the videoconference link. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'd just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I just indicate for the assistance of the Prosecutor, I think that the -- I'm not sure how long the Prosecutor means to be with Dr. Definis-Gojanovic, but I can't see it being a lengthy cross-examination, so that however that places the Prosecutor for witnesses, I -- I just indicate I would think it unlikely I'd go over an hour with that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could we have some indication of how long the Defence might be in cross-examination with tomorrow's witness, the one Your Honours have just granted a pseudonym to, for planning purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Tomorrow's witness is a little more volatile. And it really depends how the -- that one there, I'm reluctant to give an estimate. I'm sorry. I shall do better than with Mr. Gusic; I can indicate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, of course. But we have to finish tomorrow's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- witness on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I think we'd be very confident to finish the witness tomorrow. It's just a question whether it's going to be a very short one, in which case they'd need another witness or not. And I can't give an undertaking that we'd be less than a day. We'll finish the witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In order to facilitate the proceedings tomorrow, I request that all the documents, if needed, should be furnished to that witness beforehand so that -- to save the time of the -- of the hearing. Yes. Well, having said that, I think the hearing for today is adjourned.
